summary_responses.response: This arXiv paper addresses how temporary miscoordination between independently scaled microservices can overload downstream services, rejecting valuable transactions and creating an opening for attackers. Standard retry mechanisms fail to protect high-priority traffic during overloads and can trigger retry storms that worsen performance. The authors propose DiffTry (Differential Retries), a simple, stateless, coordination-free mechanism that gives each priority class a different retry-attempt limit, so high-priority requests get more chances to succeed at the point of rejection. The rule makes virtually all Federal civilian service, including temporary and intermittent employment and service with the Postal Service, Postal Regulatory Commission, and certain nonappropriated fund instrumentalities, count toward the 12-month eligibility requirement. It also allows honorable active service in the Army, Navy, Air Force, Space Force, or Marine Corps to count toward that requirement, while excluding Coast Guard and Public Health Service commissioned corps service. In addition, the rule clarifies that annual and sick leave earned under authorities outside title 5 may be substituted for unpaid FMLA leave, and it removes Veterans Health Administration employees covered by 38 U.S.C. 7421 from title 5 FMLA coverage. The rule takes effect December 14, 2026, unless significant adverse comments are received by November 16, 2026, in which case OPM will withdraw the affected provisions and issue a proposed rule.
